f33.summary: The one cipher block of the Queen Mother's letter: it is said that the prince Dauphin is to go to Flanders to receive the oath of fidelity of the Low Countries for her son Anjou and stay there, that the prince de Condé is to lead the forces assembling, and that Anjou says he will go at the time Villeroy wrote and not before; but they will still name him with Montpensier in the powers of the legation to England. The letter was already in print (1899); the cipher differs from the printed text in three small places.
f33.en:
[… it being said over here that he] is to go to Flanders to receive the oath of fidelity of those of the Low
Countries for my son, and that he is to stay there; and that the prince de Condé is to lead the forces that are
assembling and do all they can for the service of my said son, who also says that he is to go there at the time you
wrote to us and not before. But we shall not fail to name him, with the said sieur de Montpensier, in the said power
of the legation to [?England].

system: Homophonic substitution on graphic signs (Greek letters, digits, invented shapes), one to three signs per letter, a small nomenclator used also for syllables, and nulls that pad the start and end of the block.
